cues.text: Type Three hypersensitivity is driven by immune complexes, made of antigen and antibody.
When innate immune cells do not clear them, they accumulate, causing inflammation and leukocyte activation.
IgG binds a soluble antigen, forming a circulating immune complex.
These are immune complex diseases. Examples include SLE and rheumatoid arthritis.
So for Type Three, the answer is immunoglobulin G.
